claims.claim: **Multimodal analgesia**, with extra analgesia and sedation before dressing care. Anxiety and distress increase analgesic need — use distraction and therapeutic play.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Itch:** emollients, cool compress and non-sedating antihistamines.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most epidermal burns need no dressing** — protect healing skin with white soft paraffin cream.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No evidence supports aloe vera or honey**; some alternatives cause harm and should be counselled against, e.g. toothpaste.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Choose the dressing by size, depth, area and moisture needed**, and by the time to the next review; follow local state guidelines where possible.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Face, epidermal or superficial dermal:** white soft paraffin several times a day after gentle soap-free cleaning; for burns to the ear or eye, consider chloramphenicol ointment.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Face, mid or deep dermal:** follow the local burns guideline or discuss with the burns service. **Keep silver dressings away from the eyes.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Perineum, epidermal or superficial dermal:** white soft paraffin several times a day. **Contamination risk** — after each bowel action, clean with a soapy solution; catheterisation may be considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other regions, epidermal:** generally no dressing; white soft paraffin, with a low-adherent dressing for comfort if needed.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Other regions, mid or deep dermal:** local burns guideline. Layers: primary silver-impregnated (e.g. Mepilex Ag) or medicated paraffin; a secondary layer to absorb moisture and secure; then a crepe bandage securement layer.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Daily changes are not generally needed** — timing depends on the product. Ensure analgesia and check for healing and infection at each change; wear gloves.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Rapid burns-service review for poor healing or infection:** warmth · new slough or necrosis · more pain, exudate or odour · friable granulation · surrounding erythema · non-advancing edges.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **No prophylactic antibiotics.** Suspected wound infection: **swab for MCS and treat as cellulitis** with empiric antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Fever is common** from the hypermetabolic and immune response — look for other causes. **TBSA over 5% may need extra infection control, including isolation.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider toxic shock syndrome** with fever, spreading erythema, haemodynamic instability or systemic symptoms such as diarrhoea — **even in burns under 10% TBSA.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Burns raise metabolic and nutritional needs:** consult a dietitian, weigh regularly, consider measuring zinc, vitamin C and vitamin A levels and supplementing them.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start nasogastric feeding early** if facial burns, injuries or comorbidities prevent adequate oral intake.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Elevate burnt areas** and watch peripheral circulation; splint to prevent contractures. **OT/physio for deep burns crossing flexor surfaces and circumferential burns.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consult the burns service if oedema compromises vascular integrity or limb function** (limb cool distal to the burn, poor capillary return).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sun safety once healed** — hat, protective clothing, sun barrier cream. **Keloid:** emollient and compression; refer to the burns service.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consult the state paediatric burns service for:** concern about home care · suspected abuse or self-inflicted burn · dressing advice not covered · infection or poor healing · limb-threatening oedema · care beyond local comfort.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** the carer can care for the burn, follow-up is assured and dressing-change follow-up is arranged (consider an outpatient burn service).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Burns - post acute care and dressings' (Last updated May 2026), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Burns_-_post_acute_care_and_dressings/, retrieved 2026-09-23
